'''Ash-e doogh'''{{efn|{{langx|fa|آش دوغ}}, {{small|[[Iranian Persian]]:}} {{IPA|fa|ˈɒːʃ‿e‿duːɢ|}}, {{small|[[Classical Persian]]:}} {{IPA|prs|ˈɑːʃ‿ɪ‿doːɣ|}}; {{langx|tg|Оши дӯғ|Oshi do‘g‘}}, {{IPA|tg|ˈɔʃɪ dɵʁ|IPA}}; {{langx|az|{{noitalic|آیران/دوگا آشی}}|Ayran/Dovga aşı}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Ash-e doogh-Yogurt Soup آش دوغ اصیل اردبیل |url=https://rozinaspersiankitchen.wordpress.com/2018/11/30/ash-doogh-azerbaijani-dovga-soup/ |website=Rozina's Persian Kitchen |date=30 November 2018 |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref>}} ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|ɑː|ʃ|eɪ|_|ˈ|d|uː|g|,_|ˌ|ɑː|ʃ|i|_|ˈ|d|oʊ|g}}) is a [[yogurt soup]] found in various parts of [[Iran]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Ash-E Doogh |url=https://persiangood.com/recipes/ash-e-doogh/ |website=Persian GOOD |date=5 October 2020 |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> like in [[Azerbaijan (Iran)|Azerbaijan]]<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.sabziblog.com/ash-e-mast-persian-yogurt-soup-with-meatballs/|title = Ash-e Mast (Persian Yogurt Soup with Meatballs)|website = Sabzi|access-date = 2016-03-26|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160320182722/http://www.sabziblog.com/ash-e-mast-persian-yogurt-soup-with-meatballs/|archive-date = 2016-03-20|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[Shiraz]],<ref name = "shiraz">{{cite web |title=Yogurt Soup |url=https://mycaldron.com/category/kitchen-for-recipes/soupaash-salads/yogurt-soup%D8%A2%D8%B4-%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA-%D8%B4%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%B2%DB%8C/ |website=My Caldron |access-date=1 October 2022}}</ref> with differing but similar ingredients.<ref name = "shiraz"/> It is a kind of [[Aush]]. Similar dishes are found all over West Asia.  It originates from the ancient city of Ardabil, located in northwestern Iran.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Tabandeh |first=Sara |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5zIDEQAAQBAJ&dq=Ash-e+doogh&pg=PA41 |title=Persian Palate: Culinary Treasures from Iran |publisher=Sara Tabandeh |language=en}}</ref>
